brand.name: Low Value Content
brand.brandWorldFormal: The Most Ancient and Most Serene Royal House of Engagement
brand.brandArchitecture: Low Value Content is the consumer brand, portal, purveyor, and maker's mark. The Royal House of Engagement is the fictional ruling institution of the Attention Economy.
brand.brandLine: Official regalia for the attention economy.

productFamilies.name: Royal Arms
productFamilies.purpose: Flagship heraldic designs that establish the fictional institution.

productFamilies.name: Orders & Titles
productFamilies.purpose: Medals, ranks, honors, houses, and ceremonial offices.

productFamilies.name: Royal Proclamations
productFamilies.purpose: Original sayings presented as decrees, petitions, notices, and appointments.

productFamilies.name: Court Uniforms
productFamilies.purpose: Restrained apparel with a small institutional mark and a larger secondary statement.

productFamilies.name: Commemorative Editions
productFamilies.purpose: Historically grounded releases tied to the lineage and Royal Calendar.

garmentSystem.launchFormat: Every launch garment uses one front print area.
garmentSystem.front: The primary declaration remains the dominant, distance-readable artwork and must stand without secondary decoration.
garmentSystem.realmThreshold: Heraldry, seals, Latin, and script appear only where an issue requires ceremonial authority or recognized standing.
garmentSystem.extendedStory: Houses, offices, reigns, titles, lineage, and QR provenance begin on product pages, hangtags, or packaging inserts.
garmentSystem.premiumOption: Sleeve marks, upper-back issue lines, and durable garment QR seals are reserved for tested future premium editions.
garmentSystem.makerMark: Low Value Content appears as the quiet maker's mark, never as the ruling identity.
garmentSystem.storefrontDisplay: The exact frontArtDisplay asset is the authoritative image throughout the storefront. Atmospheric shirt images and design studies are preserved only as concept references.

constitution.premise: The Crown governs the Attention Economy by converting attention into impressions, impressions into influence, and influence into proof of its own importance.
principles: Metrics are presumed accurate until they become inconvenient.
Brain rot is officially classified as sustained cognitive engagement.
No one is permitted to admit that nobody is paying attention.
More content is the official remedy for too much content.

hierarchy.name: The Crown
hierarchy.function: Embodies the reigning source of authority.

hierarchy.name: The Great Houses
hierarchy.function: Compete to produce, distribute, measure, and certify importance.

hierarchy.name: Ministries and Institutes
hierarchy.function: Convert prevailing conduct into policy, research, and administrative doctrine.

hierarchy.name: The Peerage
hierarchy.function: Awards territorial titles for dubious distinction.

hierarchy.name: The Orders
hierarchy.function: Grant cross-House honors for conspicuous achievement.

hierarchy.name: The Subjects
hierarchy.function: Follow, create, refresh, and occasionally attempt to log off.

houses.name: House of Prompt
houses.portfolio: AI generation, synthetic expertise, and automated creativity
houses.contradiction: The less one understands, the more confidently one produces.

houses.name: House of Scroll
houses.contradiction: Nothing is important, but everything must be seen.

houses.name: House of Influence
houses.portfolio: Status, visibility, personal brands, and public importance
houses.contradiction: Everyone is an influencer, leaving no one available to be influenced.

houses.name: House of Signal
houses.contradiction: Every decision is data-driven; the data is adjusted to support the decision.

houses.name: House of Spam
houses.portfolio: Scale, distribution, repetition, and unsolicited reach
houses.contradiction: If nobody responded, the audience was insufficiently large.

houses.name: House of Buffer
houses.portfolio: Delay, loading, postponement, and technical excuses
houses.contradiction: Everything is imminent; nothing is presently available.

preservationRules: Never delete an existing design during migration.
Never rename a commerce catalog key without an explicit migration.
Keep editable SVG files as production-design masters until final artwork replaces them.
Treat generated mockups as concept references, never as print-ready artwork.
Keep prices and Printify identifiers authoritative on the server.
Verify every old product, saying, and declared asset before switching the deployed storefront.
Use permanent owned-domain QR routes whose destinations can change without reprinting garments.
